title: Model-geometry coupling inventory

architectural_diagnosis.summary: Plane Beris-Edwards and Channel active nematics are isolated and qualified application stacks, but their model, geometry, boundary, solver, runtime, and workflow choices are still composed by application-specific types and builders.

plane_beris_edwards.physical_model: five-component Beris-Edwards Q dynamics with complete one-constant reactive, active, and distortion nematic stress

hard_couplings.description: The component root requires exactly one three-dimensional PlaneSlab with periodic axes (0,1) and bounded axis 2.
PlaneFreeSlipBoundaryConditions contains physical Q/velocity laws and derived pressure/distortion modal parity in one Plane-specific aggregate.
Shendruk coefficient resolution jointly consumes wall height, material coefficients, and the benchmark parameter request.
PlaneBerisEdwardsPhysicsSpec vertically bundles material, Shendruk parameterization, Stokes request, and friction-mode bookkeeping.
Extruded-defect-gas twist modes are validated directly against Plane nz.
Hermitian-half storage is pinned to the final qualified periodic Plane axis.
The application composes complete nematic stress directly with the free-slip Plane modal Stokes implementation.
The zero-mean/friction tangential-mode policy exists because free slip leaves uniform tangential modes unresolved; it is not a generic pressure gauge.
legacy_production, compiled_v2, and separated_canary selection and adapter construction are Plane-specific.
Plane observation, checkpoint, restart identity, diagnostics, and completion ordering use a Plane-specific workflow schema.

channel_active_nematics.physical_model: legacy rho-parameterized active-nematic Q dynamics with active-force-only Stokes forcing
channel_active_nematics.flow_system: quasistatic incompressible no-slip Channel Stokes with pressure PCG

hard_couplings.description: The component root requires a RectangularChannel whose only periodic axis is streamwise axis 0.
ChannelActiveNematicMaterialSpec derives Landau-de Gennes a,b,c from rho and packages flow coefficients in a Channel-specific model request.
ChannelBoundaryConditions freezes physical laws as legacy parity strings rather than face-attached boundary-law declarations.
The RunSpec builder freezes no dealiasing, full projected transforms, real-first execution, and full-complex storage for this Channel oracle.
The application enforces float32, flow_alignment=1, and batch_size=1 instead of lowering general model/execution declarations.
The package application hard-codes aligned_x_smooth_noise and rejects the facade's legacy snapshot initialization mode.
The application composes active-force-only forcing directly with the no-slip Channel Stokes implementation; it is not the Plane complete-stress Beris-Edwards model.
Pressure PCG iteration policy and persistent warm-start pressure state are Channel-specific execution and restart requirements.
legacy_channel and compiled_channel_v2 selection, adapter identity, and compiled bridge construction are Channel-specific.
Channel observation, checkpoint, pressure-guess restoration, diagnostics, and completion ordering use a Channel-specific workflow schema.

model_geometry_matrix.interpretation: A Channel geometry swap is not presently valid because its force law, wall-axis derivative parity, Stokes solver, and pressure path have not been lowered or qualified for the complete-stress model.
The current Channel model is a distinct scientific model, not a geometry variant of the Plane complete-stress application.

cross_application_gaps.gap: No common EquationSystemSpec declares the production Q evolution, constitutive force law, algebraic Stokes request, fields, and diagnostics independently of geometry.
No common SimulationSpec composes model, geometry, boundaries, initial condition, numerics, integrator, execution, workflow, and invocation identities.
No capability resolver validates a model/system requirement against geometry, boundary, basis, and solver capabilities and then selects an exact lowering.
Plane and Channel boundary declarations have different representations and mix physical laws with derived modal choices to different degrees.
Applications still own model-specific metadata assembly, initial-condition selection, runtime construction, and geometry-specific solver wiring.
Runtime and checkpoint adapter identities are application-specific; this is currently safe but prevents a shared composition root.
There is no explicit unsupported-combination report explaining why a requested model, geometry, boundary assignment, and numerical policy cannot be lowered.

BoundaryAssignment: physical laws attached to field components and geometric faces
SimulationSpec: scientific, discretization, execution, and run identities
CapabilityLowering: geometry-specific Poisson, Helmholtz, Stokes, and Schur implementation selection
ApplicationPresetAdapter: no independent PDE or solver logic

migration_constraints: Existing Plane and Channel applications remain qualified compatibility presets and rollback oracles.
No migration may silently substitute the Channel active-force model for complete-stress Beris-Edwards or vice versa.
Physical boundary laws remain distinct from FFT, DCT, DST, parity, lifting, and tau implementation choices.
Geometry-specific Stokes and Schur solvers remain first-class implementations selected by exact capabilities.
Unsupported model-geometry-boundary combinations fail before tensor allocation and never fall back silently.
Hot loops receive lowered immutable plans and direct callables; they do not perform registry or capability lookup.
Scientific, discretization, execution, and run identities remain separate and restart validation remains fail-closed.
Legacy and compiled defaults do not change during P7.7 declaration and lowering work.
P7.7 introduces no new physical boundary condition and does not begin Phase 8.

next_slice.name: geometry-neutral equation-system declarations
allowed_scope_when_authorized: Introduce tensor-free field, model, constitutive-force, and algebraic-system declarations.
Express the two existing physical models honestly as distinct declarations.
Add compatibility adapters from existing Plane and Channel component graphs.
Keep runtime construction, numerical output, public facades, and defaults unchanged.
entrance_gates: This P7.7.0 inventory and its source-identity tests pass.
The two currently qualified model-geometry combinations remain explicit.
Public Plane and Channel API signatures are frozen as compatibility surfaces.
exit_gates: Every declared field and parameter has one owner.
No declaration imports Torch, transforms, runtime, workflows, applications, or geometry-specific solvers.
Existing Plane and Channel metadata can be reconstructed without loss.
No runtime path or production default changes.
